about.title: Antioch Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing someone suddenly reshapes everything, and the practical questions that follow can feel impossible to face. Antioch families facing this often find the hardest part is not knowing where to begin. That is why we are here. We handle wrongful death claims directly. We listen to what happened and help you understand your options. In 2025, Antioch recorded 293 injury collisions and 9 traffic deaths, with public records showing the heaviest crash volume along SR-4, Lone Tree Way and Hillcrest Avenue. Not every wrongful death involves a vehicle, though. Workplace incidents, unsafe premises, defective products and medical errors can all lead to a claim. Under California law, a spouse, domestic partner or child generally has the first right to file, and the deadline is two years from the date of death, shorter if a public agency is involved. We can explain who qualifies, what losses may be recovered and how the civil claim stands apart from any criminal case.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing, giving a spouse, domestic partner and children the first right, then certain dependents and heirs. We can tell you quickly where your family fits.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county or state agency may be responsible. Acting promptly protects that timeline.

items.title: A full picture of your losses
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Our family member died in a crash on SR-4 near Antioch. Does it matter who owned or maintained the road?
items.answer: It can. If a government entity such as Caltrans, the county or the city may share responsibility, California requires a claim to be presented to that agency on a much shorter timeline than the standard two years. We can review the collision report and identify every party involved before any deadline passes.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that runs separately from any criminal prosecution in Contra Costa County. The two cases have different goals and different standards of proof, and a criminal outcome, whichever way it goes, does not decide your civil claim. We can advise on how the two may interact.

items.question: How much does it cost to get a free case review?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer free consultations on wrongful death claims. We handle these cases on contingency, which means no attorney fee unless there is a recovery.
